prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: العربية · المنتجات (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 4 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "المنتج" · longest unbreakable word 50px · one-line width 97px
  col 2: header "السعر" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 70px
  col 3: header "المخزون" · longest unbreakable word 53px · one-line width 53px
  col 4: header "الوصف" · longest unbreakable word 57px · one-line width 445px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A compact Arabic product-inventory table for scanning products, comparing prices and stock, and reading a short description as supporting detail.","reading":"Right-to-left, row by row: the reader first identifies the product on the right, then checks price and stock for comparison, and finally reads the description. The numeric columns need to align cleanly for quick vertical comparison.","groups":["Columns 2 and 3 (price and stock) form a numeric comparison pair and should remain adjacent and intact.","Columns 1 and 4 (product and description) both identify the item, but the product name is the primary label and the description is secondary detail."],"keep_intact":["Price values including thousands separators and the currency marker (e.g. 3,200 ر.س)","Stock integers","Column headers","No mid-word breaks in Arabic words"],"may_wrap":["Product names at spaces","Description text at spaces"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[72,91,74,122],"idea":"Description-first: keep price and stock fully intact, give the description the largest share, and let product names wrap to two or three lines."},{"name":"B","widths":[96,91,74,98],"idea":"Balanced scan: preserve intact numeric columns while giving product and description comparable space, so product names wrap less and descriptions remain readable."},{"name":"C","widths":[116,91,74,78],"idea":"Product-first: nearly full one-line product names with price and stock protected, accepting a minimum-width description column where descriptions wrap into taller cells."}]}
